Let the tetrahedron be \(ABCD\), with \(M\) the midpoint of \(AB\) and \(N\) the midpoint of opposite edge \(CD\).

Unfold the two adjacent faces \(ABC\) and \(ACD\) along their common edge \(AC\). In the plane, take
\[
A=(0,0),\quad C=(1,0),\quad B=\left(\frac12,\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right),\quad D=\left(\frac12,-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right).
\]
Then
\[
M=\left(\frac14,\frac{\sqrt3}{4}\right),\qquad N=\left(\frac34,-\frac{\sqrt3}{4}\right).
\]
The straight-line distance in the unfolding is
\[
MN=\sqrt{\left(\frac34-\frac14\right)^2+\left(-\frac{\sqrt3}{4}-\frac{\sqrt3}{4}\right)^2}
=\sqrt{\left(\frac12\right)^2+\left(\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)^2}
=1.
\]
This straight segment crosses \(AC\) at its midpoint, so it gives a valid surface path. Other possible unfoldings give no shorter distance.

\[
\boxed{1}
\]
